sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye sthitā yatra hanyante mama putrakāḥ vyāyacchamānāḥ samare kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When my dear sons, standing in their very midst and struggling hard in battle, are slain there—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: bhīṣmaś ca nihato yatra lokanāthaḥ pratāpavān śikhaṇḍinaṃ samāsādya mṛgendra iva jambukam
english: When Bhīṣma too, lord of the world and full of valor, was struck down there—meeting Śikhaṇḍin as a lion might meet a jackal—what is this but fate?

sanskrit: droṇaś ca brāhmaṇo yatra sarvaśastrāstrapāragaḥ nihataḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃkhye kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When Droṇa too, the brāhmaṇa, master of every weapon and missile, was slain by the Pāṇḍavas in the fray—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: bhūriśravā hato yatra somadattaś ca saṃyuge bāhlīkaś ca mahārāja kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When Bhūriśravas was slain there, and Somadatta in the combat, and Bāhlīka too, O great king—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇo hato yatra jalasaṃdhaś ca kauravaḥ śrutāyuś cācyutāyuś ca kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When Sudakṣiṇa was slain there, and Jalasaṃdha the Kaurava, and Śrutāyus and Acyutāyus—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: bṛhadbalo hato yatra māgadhaś ca mahābalaḥ āvantyo nihato yatra trigartaś ca janādhipaḥ saṃśaptakāś ca bahavaḥ kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When Bṛhadbala was slain there, and the mighty king of Magadha, when the lord of Avanti fell, and the Trigarta ruler of men, and the many Saṃśaptakas—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: alaṃbusas tathā rājan rākṣasaś cāpy alāyudhaḥ ārśyaśṛṅgaś ca nihataḥ kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: And Alaṃbusa likewise, O king, and the rākṣasa Alāyudha, and Ārśyaśṛṅga slain—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: nārāyaṇā hatā yatra gopālā yuddhadurmadāḥ mlecchāś ca bahusāhasrāḥ kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When the Nārāyaṇa cowherds, frenzied for battle, were slain there, and the mlecchas in their many thousands—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: śakuniḥ saubalo yatra kaitavyaś ca mahābalaḥ nihataḥ sabalo vīraḥ kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When Śakuni, Subala's son, and the mighty hero, son of the gambler, were slain there together with their host—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ nihatā bahavo yatra kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When kings and princes, valiant men with arms like iron bars, were slain there in their numbers—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: nānādeśasamāvṛttāḥ kṣatriyā yatra saṃjaya nihatāḥ samare sarve kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When the kṣatriyas gathered from many lands, O Saṃjaya, were all slain there in the battle—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: putrāś ca me vinihatāḥ pautrāś caiva mahābalāḥ vayasyā bhrātaraś caiva kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When my sons have been struck down, and my mighty grandsons too, and my companions and brothers—what is this but the working of fate?

sanskrit: bhāgadheyasamāyukto dhruvam utpadyate naraḥ yaś ca bhāgyasamāyuktaḥ sa śubhaṃ prāpnuyān naraḥ
english: Surely a man is born endowed with his own portion of fate; and the man who is blessed with good fortune attains what is auspicious.

sanskrit: ahaṃ viyuktaḥ svair bhāgyaiḥ putraiś caiveha saṃjaya katham adya bhaviṣyāmi vṛddhaḥ śatruvaśaṃ gataḥ
english: But I am sundered from my own good fortune and from my sons, O Saṃjaya. How shall I live on now, an old man fallen into the power of my foes?

sanskrit: nānyad atra paraṃ manye vanavāsād ṛte prabho so 'haṃ vanaṃ gamiṣyāmi nirbandhur jñātisaṃkṣaye
english: I can think of nothing better in this, my lord, than to dwell in the forest. So I shall go to the forest, kinless now that my kinsmen are destroyed.

sanskrit: na hi me 'nyad bhavec chreyo vanābhyupagamād ṛte imām avasthāṃ prāptasya lūnapakṣasya saṃjaya
english: For nothing else could be better for me than to retire to the forest, fallen as I am into this plight, my wings shorn away, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: duryodhano hato yatra śalyaś ca nihato yudhi duḥśāsano viśastaś ca vikarṇaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: When Duryodhana has been slain there, and Śalya struck down in the fight, and Duḥśāsana hacked apart, and the mighty Vikarṇa as well—

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi bhīmasenasya śroṣye 'haṃ śabdam uttamam ekena samare yena hataṃ putraśataṃ mama
english: how shall I bear to hear the boastful cry of Bhīmasena, by whom alone in battle my hundred sons were slain?

sanskrit: asakṛd vadatas tasya duryodhanavadhena ca duḥkhaśokābhisaṃtapto na śroṣye paruṣā giraḥ
english: As he proclaims it again and again, with the slaying of Duryodhana too, scorched by grief and sorrow I shall not be able to endure his harsh words.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa śokasaṃtaptaḥ pārthivo hatabāndhavaḥ muhur muhur muhyamānaḥ putrādhibhir abhiplutaḥ
english: Thus the king, scorched by sorrow, his kinsmen slain, swooning again and again, overwhelmed by anguish for his sons,

sanskrit: vilapya suciraṃ kālaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya cintayitvā parābhavam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, having lamented for a long while, drawing long and burning sighs and brooding upon his defeat,

sanskrit: duḥkhena mahatā rājā saṃtapto bharatarṣabha punar gāvalgaṇiṃ sūtaṃ paryapṛcchad yathātatham
english: the king, scorched by great sorrow, O bull of the Bhāratas, once more questioned in due order Saṃjaya, the son of Gavalgaṇa, the bard:

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇau hatau śrutvā sūtaputraṃ ca pātitam senāpatiṃ praṇetāraṃ kim akurvata māmakāḥ
english: "Having heard that Bhīṣma and Droṇa were slain, and that the charioteer's son was brought down, what commander, what leader did my men then appoint?

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ senāpraṇetāraṃ yudhi kurvanti māmakāḥ acireṇaiva kālena taṃ taṃ nighnanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Whomever my men make leader of the host in battle, him in but a little while the Pāṇḍavas strike down.

sanskrit: raṇamūrdhni hato bhīṣmaḥ paśyatāṃ vaḥ kirīṭinā evam eva hato droṇaḥ sarveṣām eva paśyatām
english: At the head of the battle Bhīṣma was slain by the Diademed One before your very eyes; in just the same way Droṇa too was slain before the eyes of all.

sanskrit: evam eva hataḥ karṇaḥ sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān sa rājakānāṃ sarveṣāṃ paśyatāṃ vaḥ kirīṭinā
english: And in just the same way Karṇa, the valiant son of the charioteer, was slain by the Diademed One before the eyes of all you princes.

sanskrit: pūrvam evāham ukto vai vidureṇa mahātmanā duryodhanāparādhena prajeyaṃ vinaśiṣyati
english: Long ago I was told by the great-souled Vidura: through the wrongdoing of Duryodhana this people shall be destroyed.

sanskrit: ke cin na samyak paśyanti mūḍhāḥ samyak tathāpare tad idaṃ mama mūḍhasya tathābhūtaṃ vacaḥ sma ha
english: Some, being deluded, do not see rightly, while others see rightly; and for me, deluded as I was, that very word of his has come to pass just so.

sanskrit: yad abravīn me dharmātmā viduro dīrghadarśivān tat tathā samanuprāptaṃ vacanaṃ satyavādinaḥ
english: What the righteous, far-seeing Vidura spoke to me—that word of the truth-teller has now come to pass exactly so.

sanskrit: daivopahatacittena yan mayāpakṛtaṃ purā anayasya phalaṃ tasya brūhi gāvalgaṇe punaḥ
english: Of the wrong I did of old, my mind undone by fate—of that misrule tell me the fruit once more, O son of Gavalgaṇa.

sanskrit: ko vā mukham anīkānām āsīt karṇe nipātite arjunaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca ko vā pratyudyayau rathī
english: Who stood at the forefront of the armies when Karṇa had fallen? And what warrior went forth to meet Arjuna and Vāsudeva?

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ madrarājasya saṃyuge vāmaṃ ca yoddhukāmasya ke vā vīrasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Who guarded the right wheel of the king of Madra in the combat, and who the left, and who stood at the back of that hero eager to fight?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca vaḥ sametānāṃ madrarājo mahābalaḥ nihataḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃkhye putro vā mama saṃjaya
english: And how, when you were all gathered together, was the mighty king of Madra slain by the Pāṇḍavas in the fray—and how my son, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: brūhi sarvaṃ yathātattvaṃ bharatānāṃ mahākṣayam yathā ca nihataḥ saṃkhye putro duryodhano mama
english: Tell me all according to the truth, the great ruin of the Bhāratas, and how my son Duryodhana was slain in the battle;

sanskrit: pāñcālāś ca yathā sarve nihatāḥ sapadānugāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ
english: and how all the Pāñcālas were slain together with their followers, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin and the five sons of Draupadī;

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca yathā muktās tathobhau sātvatau yudhi kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca bhāradvājasya cātmajaḥ
english: and how the Pāṇḍavas escaped, and likewise the two Sātvatas in the fight, and Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman and the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: yad yathā yādṛśaṃ caiva yuddhaṃ vṛttaṃ ca sāṃpratam akhilaṃ śrotum icchāmi kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: What befell, how, and of what kind the recent battle was—I wish to hear it all in full, for you are skilled in the telling, O Saṃjaya."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahito yathā vṛtto mahān kṣayaḥ kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca samāsādya parasparam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear attentively, O king, how the great destruction came to pass when the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas met one another in battle.

sanskrit: nihate sūtaputre tu pāṇḍavena mahātmanā vidruteṣu ca sainyeṣu samānīteṣu cāsakṛt
english: When the charioteer's son had been slain by the great-souled Pāṇḍava, and the armies, scattered, had been rallied again and again,

sanskrit: vimukhe tava putre tu śokopahatacetasi bhṛśodvigneṣu sainyeṣu dṛṣṭvā pārthasya vikramam
english: and your son had turned away, his mind stricken with grief, and the troops were sorely shaken at the sight of Pārtha's prowess,

sanskrit: dhyāyamāneṣu sainyeṣu duḥkhaṃ prāpteṣu bhārata balānāṃ mathyamānānāṃ śrutvā ninadam uttamam
english: the troops brooding and sunk in misery, O Bhārata, and hearing the dreadful uproar of the hosts being churned to ruin,

sanskrit: abhijñānaṃ narendrāṇāṃ vikṛtaṃ prekṣya saṃyuge patitān rathanīḍāṃś ca rathāṃś cāpi mahātmanām
english: beholding the ensigns of the kings ravaged in the combat, and the fallen chariot-frames and chariots of the great-souled ones,

sanskrit: raṇe vinihatān nāgān dṛṣṭvā pattīṃś ca māriṣa āyodhanaṃ cātighoraṃ rudrasyākrīḍasaṃnibham
english: seeing the elephants slain in the fray and the foot-soldiers too, O venerable one, and the battlefield most terrible, like the playground of Rudra,

sanskrit: aprakhyātiṃ gatānāṃ tu rājñāṃ śatasahasraśaḥ kṛpāviṣṭaḥ kṛpo rājan vayaḥśīlasamanvitaḥ
english: as kings by the hundreds of thousands passed into oblivion—then Kṛpa, O king, filled with compassion, endowed with age and good character,

sanskrit: abravīt tatra tejasvī so 'bhisṛtya janādhipam duryodhanaṃ manyuvaśād vacanaṃ vacanakṣamaḥ
english: that man of splendor, skilled in speech, approaching the lord of men, spoke these words to Duryodhana, moved by sorrow:

sanskrit: duryodhana nibodhedaṃ yat tvā vakṣyāmi kaurava śrutvā kuru mahārāja yadi te rocate 'nagha
english: "Duryodhana, mark this that I shall say to you, O Kaurava; having heard it, act upon it, O great king, if it pleases you, O blameless one.

sanskrit: na yuddhadharmāc chreyān vai panthā rājendra vidyate yaṃ samāśritya yudhyante kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: There is no path better than the law of battle, O lord of kings—the path upon which kṣatriyas rely when they fight, O bull among kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: putro bhrātā pitā caiva svasreyo mātulas tathā saṃbandhibāndhavāś caiva yodhyā vai kṣatrajīvinā
english: Son, brother, even father, sister's son and maternal uncle alike, kinsmen and relatives all—these must be fought by one who lives by the warrior's calling.

sanskrit: vadhe caiva paro dharmas tathādharmaḥ palāyane te sma ghorāṃ samāpannā jīvikāṃ jīvitārthinaḥ
english: In slaying lies the highest duty, and in flight the gravest wrong; we who long to live have entered upon a grim way of life.

sanskrit: tatra tvāṃ prativakṣyāmi kiṃ cid eva hitaṃ vacaḥ hate bhīṣme ca droṇe ca karṇe caiva mahārathe
english: And so I shall offer you a word of counsel for your good: with Bhīṣma slain, and Droṇa, and Karṇa too, that great chariot-warrior,

sanskrit: jayadrathe ca nihate tava bhrātṛṣu cānagha lakṣmaṇe tava putre ca kiṃ śeṣaṃ paryupāsmahe
english: and Jayadratha struck down, and your brothers, O blameless one, and Lakṣmaṇa your son—what remnant is left to us to rely upon?

sanskrit: yeṣu bhāraṃ samāsajya rājye matim akurmahi te saṃtyajya tanūr yātāḥ śūrā brahmavidāṃ gatim
english: Those upon whom we laid our burden and set our hopes of sovereignty—those heroes, casting off their bodies, have gone to the goal of the knowers of Brahman.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tv iha vinābhūtā guṇavadbhir mahārathaiḥ kṛpaṇaṃ vartayiṣyāma pātayitvā nṛpān bahūn
english: But we, here bereft of those gifted great chariot-warriors, shall lead a wretched existence, having brought down many kings.

sanskrit: sarvair api ca jīvadbhir bībhatsur aparājitaḥ kṛṣṇanetro mahābāhur devair api durāsadaḥ
english: Even were they all yet living, Bībhatsu remains unconquered—dark-eyed, mighty-armed, hard to assail even by the gods—

sanskrit: indrakārmukavajrābham indraketum ivocchritam vānaraṃ ketum āsādya saṃcacāla mahācamūḥ
english: and confronting that ape-bannered standard, raised on high like Indra's banner and gleaming like Indra's bow and thunderbolt, the great host has trembled.

sanskrit: siṃhanādena bhīmasya pāñcajanyasvanena ca gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣāt saṃhṛṣyanti manāṃsi naḥ
english: At the lion's roar of Bhīma, at the blast of the Pāñcajanya, and at the thunder of the Gāṇḍīva, our hearts stand on end with dread.

sanskrit: carantīva mahāvidyun muṣṇanti nayanaprabhām alātam iva cāviddhaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ samadṛśyata
english: The Gāṇḍīva, like a great lightning ranging the sky, robs the eyes of their light, and is seen whirling like a brandished firebrand.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadavicitraṃ ca dhūyamānaṃ mahad dhanuḥ dṛśyate dikṣu sarvāsu vidyud abhraghaneṣv iva
english: That great bow, adorned with gold and shaken in his grip, is seen in every quarter like lightning amid massed clouds.

sanskrit: uhyamānaś ca kṛṣṇena vāyuneva balāhakaḥ tāvakaṃ tad balaṃ rājann arjuno 'stravidāṃ varaḥ gahanaṃ śiśire kakṣaṃ dadāhāgnir ivotthitaḥ
english: Borne along by Kṛṣṇa as a cloud is borne by the wind, Arjuna, O king, the foremost of those who know weapons, consumed that army of yours as a fire risen up devours dense, dry brushwood in the cold season.

sanskrit: gāhamānam anīkāni mahendrasadṛśaprabham dhanaṃjayam apaśyāma caturdantam iva dvipam
english: We beheld Dhanaṃjaya, splendid as great Indra, plunging through the ranks like a four-tusked elephant.

sanskrit: vikṣobhayantaṃ senāṃ te trāsayantaṃ ca pārthivān dhanaṃjayam apaśyāma nalinīm iva kuñjaram
english: We beheld Dhanaṃjaya throwing your army into turmoil and terrifying the kings, like an elephant ravaging a lotus-pond.

sanskrit: trāsayantaṃ tathā yodhān dhanur ghoṣeṇa pāṇḍavam bhūya enam apaśyāma siṃhaṃ mṛgagaṇā iva
english: Again we beheld that Pāṇḍava terrifying the warriors with the twang of his bow, as herds of deer behold a lion.

sanskrit: sarvalokamaheṣvāsau vṛṣabhau sarvadhanvinām āmuktakavacau kṛṣṇau lokamadhye virejatuḥ
english: Those two great archers of all the world, those bulls among all bowmen, the two dark heroes clad in their armor, shone forth in the midst of the host.

sanskrit: adya saptadaśāhāni vartamānasya bhārata saṃgrāmasyātighorasya vadhyatāṃ cābhito yudhi
english: This is now the seventeenth day, O Bhārata, of this most terrible battle that wears on, as men are slain on every side in the fighting.

sanskrit: vāyuneva vidhūtāni tavānīkāni sarvaśaḥ śaradambhodajālāni vyaśīryanta samantataḥ
english: Your armies, scattered on every hand as if by the wind, have been broken apart all around like a web of autumn clouds.

sanskrit: tāṃ nāvam iva paryastāṃ bhrāntavātāṃ mahārṇave tava senāṃ mahārāja savyasācī vyakampayat
english: Like a ship overturned and storm-tossed upon the great sea, the Ambidextrous One set your army shuddering, O great king.

sanskrit: kva nu te sūtaputro 'bhūt kva nu droṇaḥ sahānugaḥ ahaṃ kva ca kva cātmā te hārdikyaś ca tathā kva nu duḥśāsanaś ca bhrātā te bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ kva nu
english: Where then was the charioteer's son for you, and where Droṇa with his followers? Where was I, and where your own self, and where the son of Hṛdika? And where Duḥśāsana your brother, together with your brothers—where were they all?

sanskrit: bāṇagocarasaṃprāptaṃ prekṣya caiva jayadratham saṃbandhinas te bhrātṝṃś ca sahāyān mātulāṃs tathā
english: For seeing Jayadratha come within range of his arrows, and your kinsmen and brothers, your allies and your maternal uncles,

sanskrit: sarvān vikramya miṣato lokāṃś cākramya mūrdhani jayadratho hato rājan kiṃ nu śeṣam upāsmahe
english: overpowering them all and treading upon the worlds before our very eyes, Jayadratha was slain, O king—what remnant then do we rely upon?

sanskrit: ko veha sa pumān asti yo vijeṣyati pāṇḍavam tasya cāstrāṇi divyāni vividhāni mahātmanaḥ gāṇḍīvasya ca nirghoṣo vīryāṇi harate hi naḥ
english: What man is there here who shall vanquish that Pāṇḍava? The manifold divine weapons of that great-souled one, and the thunder of the Gāṇḍīva, rob us of our valor.

sanskrit: naṣṭacandrā yathā rātriḥ seneyaṃ hatanāyakā nāgabhagnadrumā śuṣkā nadīvākulatāṃ gatā
english: Like a night whose moon has vanished is this army, its leaders slain; like a dried-up river whose trees are broken by elephants, it has fallen into disarray.

sanskrit: dhvajinyāṃ hatanetrāyāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ śvetavāhanaḥ cariṣyati mahābāhuḥ kakṣe 'gnir iva saṃjvalan
english: With our banner-host bereft of its leaders, the mighty-armed warrior of the white steeds will range at will, like a fire blazing through the brushwood.

sanskrit: sātyakeś caiva yo vego bhīmasenasya cobhayoḥ dārayeta girīn sarvāñ śoṣayeta ca sāgarān
english: The onrush of both Sātyaki and Bhīmasena could rend asunder all the mountains and dry up the very seas.

sanskrit: uvāca vākyaṃ yad bhīmaḥ sabhāmadhye viśāṃ pate kṛtaṃ tat sakalaṃ tena bhūyaś caiva kariṣyati
english: The vow that Bhīma uttered in the midst of the assembly, O lord of peoples—the whole of it he has fulfilled, and yet more will he do.

sanskrit: pramukhasthe tadā karṇe balaṃ pāṇḍavarakṣitam durāsadaṃ tathā guptaṃ gūḍhaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: With Karṇa once stationed in the van, the army the Pāṇḍavas guarded was unassailable—warded and hidden as it was by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: yuṣmābhis tāni cīrṇāni yāny asādhūni sādhuṣu akāraṇakṛtāny eva teṣāṃ vaḥ phalam āgatam
english: Those evil deeds that you wrought against the good, done without cause—the fruit of them has now come upon you.

sanskrit: ātmano 'rthe tvayā loko yatnataḥ sarva āhṛtaḥ sa te saṃśayitas tāta ātmā ca bharatarṣabha
english: For your own sake you gathered the whole world by every effort; yet now that world, and your own life as well, are in peril, my son, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: rakṣa duryodhanātmānam ātmā sarvasya bhājanam bhinne hi bhājane tāta diśo gacchati tadgatam
english: Guard your own self, Duryodhana, for the self is the vessel of all; for once the vessel is broken, my son, that which it held flows away to every quarter.

sanskrit: hīyamānena vai saṃdhiḥ paryeṣṭavyaḥ samena ca vigraho vardhamānena nītir eṣā bṛhaspateḥ
english: He who is waning, or equal in strength, should seek a treaty; he who is growing in power may make war—such is the policy of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pāṇḍuputrebhyo hīnāḥ svabalaśaktitaḥ atra te pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃdhiṃ manye kṣamaṃ prabho
english: We, then, are inferior to the sons of Pāṇḍu in the strength of our own forces; herein I judge a treaty with the Pāṇḍavas to be the fitting course, my lord."
